# Original HLS test media

Generated offline with FFmpeg 9.0.2 from color and sine sources; no third-party
media was used. From the repository root, generate each set with:

```sh
ffmpeg -nostdin -hide_banner -loglevel error -f lavfi -i color=c=blue:s=32x32:r=10:d=1.8 -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=48000:duration=1.8 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -g 6 -threads 1 -c:a aac -b:a 32k -hls_time 0.6 -hls_list_size 0 -hls_segment_filename tests/fixtures/hls/ts/segment-%d.ts -y tests/fixtures/hls/ts/index.m3u8
ffmpeg -nostdin -hide_banner -loglevel error -f lavfi -i color=c=blue:s=32x32:r=10:d=1.8 -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=48000:duration=1.8 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -g 6 -threads 1 -c:a aac -b:a 32k -hls_time 0.6 -hls_list_size 0 -hls_segment_type fmp4 -hls_segment_filename tests/fixtures/hls/fmp4/segment-%d.m4s -y tests/fixtures/hls/fmp4/index.m3u8
```

`range/combined.mp4` concatenates fMP4 `init.mp4` followed by the three media
fragments. Its playlist describes the exact initialization and segment byte
lengths: an explicit first media offset followed by implicit continuation offsets.
When regenerating, derive those ranges from the resulting file lengths.

Required tests verify exact assembled bytes. With `YT_DLP_RS_TEST_FFPROBE` set,
the same test also confirms H.264 video and AAC audio in TS, fMP4 and byte-range
output. No live sites or runtime Python fallback are involved.

The `aes-ts`, `aes-fmp4`, `aes-range` and `aes-keys` directories are generated by
`python3 tools/generate_hls_aes_fixtures.py` using OpenSSL/LibreSSL AES-128-CBC
with PKCS#7 padding and no salt wrapper. Original generation used LibreSSL 3.3.6.
The two keys are public test constants: consecutive byte values 0–15 and 16–31.
They are original fixture data, never production credentials. TS uses implicit
IVs 7 and 8, then rotates key and IV. fMP4 uses explicit IV 2 for initialization
and initial media, then rotates. The range fixture concatenates those independently
encrypted fMP4 resources and declares exact ciphertext ranges.

Required tests decrypt and compare the exact original clear fixture bytes; the
same FFprobe option verifies tracks in all three encrypted outputs. OpenSSL and
Python are regeneration tools only and are unnecessary at runtime or in tests.

The `audio-video` directory contains separate original video-only H.264 TS and
audio-only AAC/ADTS resources generated with FFmpeg 9.0.2. Its handwritten master
references the audio group `main`, NAME English, LANGUAGE en and DEFAULT/AUTOSELECT
YES. Regenerate the resources from the repository root:

```sh
ffmpeg -nostdin -hide_banner -loglevel error -f lavfi -i color=c=blue:s=32x32:r=10:d=1.8 -an -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -g 6 -threads 1 -hls_time 0.6 -hls_list_size 0 -hls_segment_filename tests/fixtures/hls/audio-video/video/segment-%d.ts -y tests/fixtures/hls/audio-video/video/index.m3u8
ffmpeg -nostdin -hide_banner -loglevel error -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=48000:duration=1.8 -vn -c:a aac -b:a 32k -threads 1 -f segment -segment_time 0.6 -segment_list_type m3u8 -segment_list tests/fixtures/hls/audio-video/audio/index.m3u8 -y tests/fixtures/hls/audio-video/audio/segment-%d.aac
ffmpeg -nostdin -hide_banner -loglevel error -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=48000:duration=1.8 -vn -c:a aac -b:a 32k -threads 1 -f mpegts -y tests/fixtures/hls/audio-video/audio/track.ts
```

The standalone AAC-in-TS asset additionally verifies the local TS audio demuxer.
The real merged MP4 tests check H.264 and AAC tracks with AAC codec extradata.
